p: Cheltenham is a town that loves an occasion. Its calendar is packed with festivals covering jazz, science, music and literature, and big race weeks at the racecourse draw huge crowds too. During those busy spells, hotels, restaurants and activities all get booked up quickly, so if your visit lines up with one, sort your escape room slot well in advance rather than hoping to wander in.

Once you're inside, the golden rule is communication. Say what you've found, even if it seems pointless, because the clue you think is rubbish might be exactly what someone else needs. Try not to get fixated on one puzzle; rooms usually have several threads running at once, and moving on often unlocks the one you were stuck on. A fresh pair of eyes can do wonders. If you can, have a quick look at the room themes beforehand so you pick one that suits the ages and nerves in your group.

Around the town, there's plenty to fill the rest of the day. Imperial Gardens, near the Promenade, are a riot of colour in the warmer months and a lovely place to sit with a coffee. The Wilson, Cheltenham's art gallery and museum, is a short walk from the centre and well worth an hour. Head a little further north and you'll find Pittville Park, with its lake, play areas and the elegant Pittville Pump Room, a reminder of the town's spa heritage. And if you've got the car, the Cotswolds are right on the doorstep: Cleeve Hill, just outside town, gives you sweeping views across to the Malverns on a clear day.
